clue.text: A protein compounded of poison

indicators.note: a compound is made by mixing things, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that a certain protein is made up of toxic matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compounded of' rearranges the eight letters of A PROTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid found in deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Those left take it easy

explanation.surface: The people remaining behind can relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest are the remainder of a group; to rest is to relax or put your feet up.

clue.text: Take advantage of one married model

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: A married fashion model is accused of exploiting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose on someone is to exploit their good nature.

clue.text: Wagons fronting small house with oak panelling

indicators.note: the wagons are placed at the front, before the small house

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon
a cot is a small cottage

explanation.surface: Farm carts stand in front of a little cottage with wooden walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling lining the lower part of a room's walls, traditionally of oak.

clue.text: Genius demands expert attention

parts.note: a master is an expert in a craft
to pay mind is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A brilliant person insists on skilled care.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastermind is a person of outstanding intellect, a brilliant planner.

clue.text: Dereliction of duty makes top officer scowl

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer, the officer in charge
to pout is to pull a sulky face

explanation.surface: A commander glowers at someone who has shirked their responsibilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion of a responsibility, a failure to do what is required.

clue.text: Flag flying when sovereign is on board

definitions.text: Flag flying when sovereign is on board

parts.words: Flag flying when sovereign is on board
parts.note: suggests a royal standard hoisted on a ship carrying the monarch, but read as a long narrow pennant flown at a masthead

explanation.surface: A banner is raised on the ship when the monarch comes aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pictures a royal ensign, but the answer is simply a long pennant that flutters from a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant flown from a masthead.

clue.text: Right to take a meal containing vegetable

parts.note: a dish is a prepared course of food

explanation.surface: Someone has a right to a meal that includes greens.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a crisp root eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Militant female banker in s.America

explanation.surface: A fierce woman works for a bank in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Amazons were a race of women warriors; the Amazon is the great South American river, which has banks.

clue.text: Spring lock

explanation.surface: A spring-loaded catch that secures a door.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to leap or dash off suddenly; a bolt is a sliding bar that fastens a door.

clue.text: Arrangement welcomed by aspiring priest

explanation.surface: A would-be cleric is pleased by the plans made for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordination can mean the act of putting things in order, and also the ceremony that makes someone a minister of the church.

clue.text: Little time to publish paper

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to issue a book or magazine is to publish it

explanation.surface: There is hardly any time left to bring out the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin soft paper, as in tissue paper or a paper handkerchief.

clue.text: Sort of effort needed to push manure around

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Shifting a heap of dung takes enormous exertion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the ten letters of PUSH MANURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhuman effort is one beyond normal human capability.

clue.text: Model city sure to offer peace of mind

indicators.note: to model clay is to shape it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An ideal town promises residents freedom from worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like an adjective (a model city) but it is the anagram signal on CITY SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Security is freedom from danger or anxiety, a feeling of safety.

clue.text: Seeing if I lapse in any way

indicators.note: in any way at all, meaning in any order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone worries about being noticed if they slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in any way' rearranges the six letters of I LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or the act of catching sight of something.

clue.text: Roused by lad after a funeral party

indicators.note: the lad is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a wake is a gathering held after a funeral
Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone was woken by a boy coming home from a funeral gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Awakened means roused from sleep, stirred into consciousness.

clue.text: Short way to travel on foot

definitions.text: Short way to travel on foot

parts.note: ST is the short form of street, a way
to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A brief walking distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a single long step, the short distance covered on foot in one pace.

clue.text: Notes union with outpouring of emotion

parts.note: E and F are two musical notes
fusion is a joining together into one

explanation.surface: A love song about a marriage brings a flood of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: An effusion is an unrestrained gushing of words or feelings.

clue.text: Boy returned to old city by circuitous route

indicators.note: returned means the word is read back the other way

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name
Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A lad went back to an ancient city by a roundabout road.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a longer roundabout way taken to avoid something.

clue.text: Reduce iron production

explanation.surface: Steelworks should cut their output of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as DE-CREASE: to iron is to take creases out.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrease is to lessen; pressing a garment with an iron removes its creases.

clue.text: Each loop that is fastened to a sail

definitions.text: that is fastened to a sail

parts.note: a ring is a closed loop

explanation.surface: Every ring is tied on to the canvas of a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: An earing is a small line used to fasten the corner of a sail to a yard or spar.

clue.text: Ways heartless fay uses to adapt

parts.note: modi is the Latin plural of modus, a way or method

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word fay is taken out

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted fairy has methods she uses to change things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the A from FAY, leaving FY. A fay is a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify is to alter something to suit new conditions.

clue.text: French husband born at sea

parts.note: mari is French for husband
né is French for born, as in a man's former name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's spouse was delivered on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine means relating to or found in the sea.

clue.text: Complain more noisily in game reserve

parts.note: to grouse is to grumble

indicators.note: said noisily, out loud, the word more is heard as a sound-alike

parts.note: more sounds like a stretch of upland heath

explanation.surface: Someone moans ever louder about a wildlife park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' signals that MORE is heard as MOOR. A grouse moor is British upland heath kept for shooting the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse moor is moorland managed for shooting grouse, a game bird.

clue.text: Unlikely to lose colour quickly

explanation.surface: A dye that will not wash out, done rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour-fast dye does not run or fade; fast also means rapidly.

clue.text: Even it's home

explanation.surface: Even a modest dwelling is a residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means level and smooth; a flat is an apartment where someone lives.

clue.text: Promise to start military action

explanation.surface: A pledge to open hostilities.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage oneself is to pledge or commit; to engage the enemy is to begin fighting them.

clue.text: Paid protesters cause barman to collapse

indicators.note: to cause something to collapse is to make it fall to pieces, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the clue as held reads barman to; the setter's fodder must be bar men to, giving an E

explanation.surface: Hired demonstrators make a pub worker faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' rearranges BAR MEN TO into RENT A MOB. As held the clue reads 'barman', which leaves an A where the E is needed: the original was surely 'bar men'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a crowd hired to demonstrate or cause trouble.
